subject: QBR: Capacity Runway & Unit-Economics Checkpoint (Exec digest)
messages:
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Maria Hernandez <maria.hernandez@bigretail.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbuscloud.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: QBR: Capacity Runway & Unit-Economics Checkpoint (Exec digest)

Team / Maria,

Quick executive digest ahead of next week’s QBR — please skim and action the three asks below by EOD tomorrow. I’m consolidating into the QBR deck Friday morning.

Summary bullets
- Runway (customer-facing capacity): estimated 9–11 weeks at current demand; sensitive to two events: enterprise promo (projected +22% peak) and one large marketplace integration (BigRetail pilot).
- GPU spend YTD: $6.1M raw; net after committed discounts: $4.9M. Primary levers left: reserved rebalancing, adaptive batching, and prefix caching improvements.
- Utilization: fleet average 68% (p95: 93% on evening peaks). Effective token cost is up ~18% QoQ driven by small-batch low-latency traffic.
- Impact of batching/caching: our sims show up to 28% unit-cost improvement if we can raise effective batch depth on medium-latency routes and deploy aggressive prefix KV caching for repeat queries. See attached sim.

Immediate asks (EOD tomorrow)
1) Karthik — confirm which non-prod slots can be reclaimed this quarter and estimated cost savings (xlsx tab: reclaim-options).
2) Vivek — call out committed capacity we can shift to burst without breaking SLAs; include cost delta and lead times (commitment_table.csv attached).
3) Irene/Prioym — pick two customers for a canary of relaxed batching (20% traffic) and a KV-cache pilot; note expected latency delta and rollback criteria.

Attachments: capacity_runway_v2.xlsx, batching_cache_sim.csv, qbr-ask-list.md

I’ll be on a short travel window but reachable. If Maria or anyone external needs clarifications, flag and we’ll loop in Solutions.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: QBR: Capacity Runway & Unit-Economics Checkpoint (Exec digest)

Thanks Lauren — quick notes inline.

> Runway (customer-facing capacity): estimated 9–11 weeks
I agree with the baseline; two clarifications: the 11-week end assumes we defer one non-critical model backfill (NLP-2) and keep current pre-warm policies. If we ship NLP-2, expected runway drops to ~7 weeks.

> Ask 1 — reclaim non-prod slots
We have ~18 non-prod slots tagged for low-priority experiments. I can identify 10 that are safe to reclaim this quarter (expected savings: ~$180k/mo). I’ll upload the reclaim matrix to the capacity workbook by EOD.
Questions:
- Does the exec deck need per-region breakout? I have EU/US split but not APAC in this tab.
Karthik
Senior Director, Serving Infrastructure

Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: Capacity Runway & Unit-Economics Checkpoint (Exec digest)

Adding committed-capacity context.

We have two reserved pools expiring next quarter (Pool A: 128 GPUs, Pool B: 64 GPUs). With current utilization patterns we can safely reassign up to 10% (approx 19 GPUs) from Pool B to burst for 8–12 weeks assuming we keep a 7-day rolling buffer for enterprise SLAs. Cost delta: shifting to burst would raise per-GPU hourly effective cost by ~16% but unlocks immediate runway value equal to ~$250k of monthly on-demand savings when applied to hot routes where batching can be increased.

On batching/caching: our profiling shows that evening peaks are dominated by small-chat short-sequence requests; if we gate those into a slightly higher batching window (50–100ms relaxed tail) we can increase mean batch depth from 6 → 11 on targeted routes and realize ~20% token-cost reduction. KV cache for repeat-inference on the marketplace partner (BigRetail) looks promising — estimated hit-rate 28% first-phase which maps to ~12% unit-cost uplift avoided.
I’ve attached commitment_table.csv with the exact pool ids and recommended rebalances.
—Vivek
Director, Capacity Planning

Thanks Lauren and team — quick external note from BigRetail.

We’d be interested in the KV-cache pilot — that 28% hit-rate looks impactful. A couple of asks on our side:
- Can Redwood guarantee no customer-facing latency regressions > 100ms for our pilot cohort (we can accept small tail increases but need <1% error rate spike).
- If you shift reserved to burst, will our current SLA change? We need confirmation before committing pilot traffic.
Happy to be the first canary customer for both batching relaxation (20% traffic) and KV cache if you can provide a short rollback window and a runbook.
Best,
Maria Hernandez
Head of Platform Ops, BigRetail

Subject: Re: QBR: Capacity Runway & Unit-Economics Checkpoint (Exec digest)

Thanks — internal decision summary and next steps.

Decision (for QBR slide):
- Approve reclaim of 10 non-prod slots (Karthik). Impact: ~ $180k/mo.
- Approve reassigning up to 10% from Pool B to burst for an initial 8-week window (Vivek) with daily SLA monitoring and a rollback threshold of 2x current P99 latency.
- Approve BigRetail for canary pilot (Irene to own runbook + rollback).
Action owners & near-term deliverables:
- Karthik: update capacity_runway_v2.xlsx with region breakout + reclaim matrix (due EOD today).
- Vivek: finalize commitment_table.csv and note lead times for rebalancing; quantify cost delta for the deck (due EOD today).
- Priyom: draft a 1-page runbook for the batching/caching canary and a simple dashboard (ok to reuse the monitoring templates under QBR drive).
I will compile a one-slide decision summary for the exec pack and tag lauren for signoff.
Irene Choi
Sr. Director, Customer Reliability
